<sub>She looks all the way round. Nothing. <span lang="ja">ｼｰﾝ</span> (shīn) is how a manga spells silence.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
<b>Castaway</b> (working title) is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, the ten-hour kind: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a pair of cream headphones. She mostly idles, nodding to the music, and more than 90 activities wait on four timers for their turn. An unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines of the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i>. Always daytime.
</p>

<div align="center">
<table>
<tr><td align="right">every 2 to 5 min</td><td align="center"><span aria-hidden="true"><span lang="ja">d⁠(⁠･⁠ω⁠･⁠)⁠b</span></span></td><td>a coconut, a jog, some fishing</td></tr>
<tr><td align="right">every 12 to 25 min</td><td align="center"><span aria-hidden="true"><span lang="ja">━</span> <span lang="ja">d⁠(⁠°⁠ω⁠°⁠)⁠b</span> <span lang="ja">━⁠!</span></span></td><td>a sea turtle drops by</td></tr>
<tr><td align="right">every 30 to 60 min</td><td align="center"><span aria-hidden="true"><b><span lang="ja">━⁠━⁠━</span> <span lang="ja">Σ⁠d⁠(⁠°⁠Д⁠°⁠)⁠b</span> <span lang="ja">━⁠━⁠━⁠!⁠!</span></b></span></td><td>a shark in headphones (see above)</td></tr>
<tr><td align="right">every 3 to 6 hours</td><td align="center"><span aria-hidden="true"><b><span lang="ja">キ⁠タ⁠━⁠━⁠━⁠━⁠━</span>​<span lang="ja">d⁠(⁠°⁠∀⁠°⁠)⁠b</span>​<span lang="ja">━⁠━⁠━⁠━⁠━⁠!⁠!⁠!⁠!</span></b></span></td><td>she walks off across the sea, and back</td></tr>
</table>
</div>

<p align="center">
<sub>Four timers, and how excited to get about each. Every gag waits for the next bar of the music, so it lands on the beat. <span lang="ja">キタ</span> (kita): "it's here!", as typed on Japanese text boards when the long-awaited thing finally happens.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
<span aria-hidden="true"><span lang="ja">♪⁠&nbsp;⁠∿⁠∿⁠∿</span></span> &nbsp;<b>every sound is synthesized from code</b>&nbsp; <span aria-hidden="true"><span lang="ja">∿⁠∿⁠∿⁠&nbsp;⁠♪</span></span><br>
<sub>No samples, no loops, no recordings: more than 150 sounds written by <a href="tools/make_audio.py">tools/make_audio.py</a>, from the 60-second theme (80 BPM, F major, electric piano and a kalimba lead) to the gulls. Nobody has heard any of it yet. <span aria-hidden="true"><span lang="ja">d⁠(⁠･⁠ω⁠･⁠)⁠b</span></span> <span lang="ja">ﾄ⁠ﾞ⁠ｷ⁠ﾄ⁠ﾞ⁠ｷ</span></sub>
</p>

```sh
python tools/serve.py      # then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
python tools/schedule.py   # validate the schedule, simulate a 10-hour run
```

<sub>She builds a sandcastle. It stays on the beach until the tide comes for it. The tide always comes for it.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
<span aria-hidden="true"><span lang="ja">ﾉ⁠━⁠━⁠━⁠&nbsp;⁠&lt;⁠゜⁠)⁠)⁠)⁠彡</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">⌒⁠━⁠━⁠━⁠⌒⁠&lt;⁠゜⁠)⁠)⁠)⁠彡</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">･⁠･⁠･</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">～⁠v⁠～</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">ﾎ⁠ﾟ⁠ﾄ⁠ｯ⁠&nbsp;⁠&lt;⁠゜⁠)⁠)⁠)⁠彡</span></span><br>
<sub>Spear fishing: a heroic lunge, a miss, and the fish take turns jumping over the spear. A gull drops one at her feet, out of pity.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
<span aria-hidden="true"><span lang="ja">d⁠(⁠･⁠ω⁠･⁠)⁠b⁠つ⁠｡</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">ﾎ⁠ﾟ⁠ﾝ⁠ﾎ⁠ﾟ⁠ﾝ</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">･⁠･⁠･</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">ψ</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">ﾆ⁠ｮ⁠ｷ⁠ﾆ⁠ｮ⁠ｷ</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">･⁠･⁠･</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">✿</span></span><br>
<sub>She plants a kumara. Hours later it has quietly grown leaves. Later still it flowers, pale lavender. It is a ten-hour video: it has time.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
<span aria-hidden="true"><span lang="ja">d⁠(⁠･⁠ω⁠･⁠)⁠b</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">ﾃ⁠ｸ⁠ﾃ⁠ｸ</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">～⁠～⁠～</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">ｼ⁠ｰ⁠ﾝ</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">～⁠～⁠～</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">ﾃ⁠ｸ⁠ﾃ⁠ｸ</span> &nbsp; <span lang="ja">d⁠(⁠˘⁠ω⁠˘⁠)⁠b⁠つ⁠□</span></span><br>
<sub>She could leave any time. She walks out across the water and out of frame, the island sits empty for twenty seconds, and she walks back with an iced coffee. Never explained.</sub>
</p>

<details>
<summary><b>the numbers</b> <span aria-hidden="true"><span lang="ja">φ⁠(⁠･⁠ω⁠･⁠)</span></span></summary>

- **The schedule.** <a href="activities.toml">activities.toml</a> lists more than 90 activities (94 on 2026-10-01, and growing). Most sit on four timers: regular every 2 to 5 minutes, occasional every 12 to 25, rare every 30 to 60, super rare every 3 to 6 hours (at most 3 a run). The rest are follow-ups that only ever come after another one. In a typical 10-hour run (median of 200 simulated runs) that is about 155 regular, 30 occasional, 13 rare and 2 super-rare events. She is busy about a third of the time and idling the rest.
- **The beat.** Every activity starts on the next bar of the music, every 3 seconds: 12,000 bars in the default 10:00:00 run (seed 1992). Lanes let things overlap, so a visitor can turn up while she is busy with something else.
- **The sound.** All of it synthesized by <a href="tools/make_audio.py">tools/make_audio.py</a>: no samples, loops or recordings, so no third-party licence applies. The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major (ii-V-I-vi), 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds: electric piano, kalimba lead, soft drums, vinyl crackle. The ocean is its own seamless 60-second loop. The mix sits at -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and levels are adjustable in master and per routine. Not yet heard by anyone.
- **The picture.** 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, always daytime. Hard cuts and stepped movement. Scene life: 26 entries, of which shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; birds, planes with vapour trails, whales, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.
- **The renderer.** A web page, <a href="web/index.html">web/index.html</a>, with live preview and export: plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages. It encodes frame-exact H.264 in the browser with WebCodecs (68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), and the server mixes the sound and joins the two into a YouTube-ready MP4.
- **The tools.** <code>python tools/serve.py</code> (preview and export), <code>python tools/schedule.py</code> (validate, simulate 10 hours), <code>python tools/render_demo.py --dev</code> (every activity in a dev reel, with a heads-up display). The working notes are in <a href="MUSING.md">MUSING.md</a>.

</details>

</p>

<p align="center">
Faces typed by the Upright Faces Society, Tiny Island Branch (membership: one, plus the cat when it visits).<br>
Bows to the turtle, for dozing; the shark, for keeping time; the crab, for wearing it well; the gull, for the fish; and the tide, for consistency.
</p>

<p align="center">
<sub>Fonts: whatever your computer had. Each character in a face may come from a different one, which is how kaomoji have always looked. In Japan an arms-up face can mean hooray, or <span lang="ja">ｵﾜﾀ</span> (owata, "it's all over"). On a desert island both readings are correct.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
<sub>Castaway is an original, unofficial project in development: no video yet, no public link, plenty of time. <i>Johnny Castaway</i> and its characters belong to their owners, and this project is not affiliated with them. The Upright Faces Society is not a real society.</sub>
</p>
